what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 3: How far apart are the static law and the formation laws in infinite volume?. GIVEN (refereed twice): on any window with a cycle the static law is NOT in the convex hull of adapted (value-dependent order) formation laws, for every non-constant rule; the indicator of the constant patterns separates them (Hoelder plus the cycle). TASK: make it quantitative and infinite-volume: (a) a lower bound on the total-variation distance between the static law and the hull that grows with the number of independent cycles; (b) positive relative-entropy density between the static law and any monotone-order formation law on Z^2 and Z^3 (so they are mutually singular in infinite volume) for the six-axis rule at (3,1,2), with an explicit lower bound; (c) which local observable shows the difference most strongly (the plaquette four-point function?) and its exact value under both laws on the 2x2 and 2x2x2 windows. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/static-formation-singularity/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/static-formation-singularity/<name>/check.py"
